summary: Dedicated burst: denials higher than expected during scheduled indexing run (Northpeak Search)
environment: prod us-east (H100 dedicated + shared burst pool)
description:
Issue summary
Northpeak Search (Dedicated) reports burst requests being denied at a much higher rate than expected during a predictable weekly indexing job. Customer expected to burst up to ~1.8x baseline for ~45 minutes; observed ~35–55% denials with 429/overload responses and throughput well below the contracted burst cap.

Impact
- Customer indexing job missed internal deadline; customer had to re-run with lower concurrency.
- Customer observed 429s and increased end-to-end job duration.
- No customer data loss. No evidence of cross-tenant impact beyond normal tail variance.

Customer expectation
- Burst enabled + configured cap should allow temporary above-baseline utilization until either (a) tenant cap reached, or (b) pool saturation triggers denials.
- If denied, customer wants deterministic and explainable reason codes.

Environment
- Dedicated tenant: northpeak-prod (tenant_id: tnt_4c1b2f) in us-east, hardware class H100.
- Baseline reserved: 16 GPUs.
- Burst enabled: yes.
- Config (as found at time of incident): max_burst_ratio=1.25, cooldown=10m, priority_tier=silver.
- Workload: embeddings + rerank batch (high RPS, short prompts, concurrency spikes).

Symptoms
- Spike in admission denials starting ~2025-05-22 16:05 UTC, lasting ~50 minutes.
- Denial reason distribution (from customer logs + gateway): BURST_TENANT_CAP_EXCEEDED and TELEMETRY_STALE dominated.

Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Increase client concurrency from 128 -> 512 workers for batch indexing.
2) Run embeddings requests at sustained high QPS for 10–15 minutes.
3) Observe increased 429s and reduced throughput even though Console shows burst pool utilization < 70%.

Evidence (customer-provided)
- Request error snippets:
  - HTTP 429 from gateway: {"code":"OVERLOADED","message":"Burst denied","burst_denial_reason":"TELEMETRY_STALE"}
  - HTTP 429 from gateway: {"code":"OVERLOADED","message":"Burst denied","burst_denial_reason":"BURST_TENANT_CAP_EXCEEDED"}
- Sample request IDs:
  - req_01HZYR7Z9YQ6T4A0H0A8E2Y3K
  - req_01HZYR82Y6D0D6XK8D5C0KQ1V

Internal quick links
- Grafana: Burst pool saturation + denials (us-east/H100)
- Grafana: Denial reasons by tenant (tnt_4c1b2f)
- Logs: burst-admission-controller use1
- Runbook: Burst pool overload mitigation

Initial hypothesis
Either (a) tenant-level cap/cooldown configured too low vs customer expectations, (b) telemetry lag causing conservative denials (TELEMETRY_STALE), or (c) routing repeatedly retries and hits cap with non-idempotent admission accounting.

resolution:
Resolved via (A) configuration correction and (B) platform hotfix.

A) Tenant configuration update (northpeak-prod / tnt_4c1b2f)
- max_burst_ratio increased from 1.25 -> 1.8 (align with onboarding expectation)
- cooldown reduced from 10m -> 2m (better fit for batch indexing pattern)
- No change to fleet safety caps or global circuit breaker.

B) Engineering fix deployed
- Rolled out telemetry smoothing / anti-flap guard to reduce conservative TELEMETRY_STALE denials under transient telemetry delays.
- Deployed in us-east admission controller, validated via dashboards (denial reason mix normalized; telemetry-stale denials down materially).

Customer-facing outcome
- Customer re-test showed sustained throughput improvement and denial rate reduced to low single digits.

Follow-ups
- Ensure CS onboarding checklist explicitly captures intended max_burst_ratio and cooldown for batch workloads (prevent default 1.25x mismatch).
- Add alert annotation/runbook step: when TELEMETRY_STALE dominates denials while pool utilization < 70%, check telemetry freshness and apply mitigation.
- Consider client guidance doc snippet: avoid synchronized retries; ramp concurrency; use jittered exponential backoff (link to docs PR once published).
